standard_prerequisites.name: The resolution property and its consequence that a perfect complex can be represented by a bounded complex of finite locally free modules, plus base change of envelopes

core_obligations: Dispose of the easy conditions: the first condition is exactly part (1) of the definition of the Chern classes, and the second implies the first because a bounded complex of finite locally free modules on X pulls back to one on Y (proof lines 9320-9322).

Show that quasi-compact irreducible components imply the first condition: view each component as a reduced integral closed subscheme, note that the disjoint union of the components maps to X by an envelope, choose for each component an envelope with an ample family of invertible modules, observe that the disjoint union of those is again an envelope, use that an ample family gives the resolution property, and represent the pulled back perfect object by a bounded complex of finite locally free modules (proof lines 9324-9340).

Dispose of the remaining conditions: quasi-compactness of X implies quasi-compactness of its irreducible components, and for the fifth condition one takes an envelope of the target over which the pulled back object is represented, notes that the base change along X -> X' is again an envelope, and that the pullback of the representing complex represents the pullback of the object (proof lines 9342-9352).
proof_roadmap: The first two conditions from the definition (proof lines 9320-9322).
Quasi-compact components give an envelope with the resolution property and hence a representing complex (proof lines 9324-9340).
Quasi-compactness and pullback along a morphism of locally finite type schemes (proof lines 9342-9352).
difficulty_reason: The lemma collects six sufficient conditions under which the Chern classes of a perfect object are defined, ranging from the existence of a trivialising envelope to quasi-compactness of the irreducible components of X and to the object being pulled back from a perfect object with defined Chern classes (statement lines 9299-9318, tag 0GUE). The first two are definitional, but the implication from quasi-compact components to the first condition is a real construction: it passes to the disjoint union of the components, builds an envelope with an ample family of invertible modules over each, verifies that the disjoint union of those envelopes is again an envelope, invokes the resolution property to represent the pulled back perfect object by a bounded complex of finite locally free modules. That construction is the substance, so the claim is H2.
